title: Country, nationality and language
subtitle: Poland - Polish - Polish; the Far East; the British
summary: Say where people come from, what nationality they are and what language they speak.

lesson.heading: Who speaks what where?
lesson.note: The nationality word and the language word are often the same, but not always: people from Brazil are Brazilian and they speak Portuguese.

lesson.heading: More countries
lesson.note: The UK is England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

lesson.heading: Talking about your country
lesson.text: Use **come from** for your country, a **nationality** word for you, and **first language** for the language you grew up with. The **capital** is the main city, and the **population** is the number of people who live there.

examples.text: The **capital** is Buenos Aires, which has a **population** of more than 10 million people.

lesson.heading: Common mistakes
lesson.text: Countries, nationalities and languages always start with a **capital letter**. Use the nationality word, not the country word, in front of a noun. And do not forget **the** in front of the UK and the USA.

lesson.heading: Parts of the world
lesson.text: The **continents** in the world are **Europe**, **Africa**, **Asia**, **North America**, **South America**, **Australia** (Australia and New Zealand) and **Antarctica**.

lesson.heading: Areas of the world
lesson.note: These names all take the except Scandinavia.

lesson.heading: The people
lesson.text: To talk about all the people of a country, add **-s** to nationalities that end in **-i** or **-(i)an**. For most other nationalities we need **the** and no -s.
lesson.note: With both groups you can also add the word people: Brazilian people, British people.

lesson.text: If the nationality word ends in -ese, -ss, -sh or -ch (Japanese, Swiss, British, French), say the + the word with no -s.

exercises.prompt: Match the country with the nationality.
What nationality are people from Thailand? They are ___.
exercises.explanation: Thailand - Thai. The nationality and the language are the same word.

exercises.prompt: What language is spoken in Spain? ___.
What language is spoken in Brazil?
exercises.explanation: People from Brazil are Brazilian, but the language is Portuguese.

exercises.prompt: Where do people speak Hebrew? In ___.
exercises.explanation: Hebrew is the language of Israel.
Mandarin (and Cantonese) is spoken in China.

exercises.prompt: What language is spoken in Egypt? ___.
exercises.hint: (one word - also spoken in Saudi Arabia)
exercises.explanation: Egypt and Saudi Arabia both use Arabic.

exercises.prompt: What part of the world is each country in?

exercises.explanation: Bangkok is the capital city of Thailand.
Athens is the capital of Greece; the people are Greek.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'We do a lot of business with ___.' (JAPAN)
exercises.explanation: Nationalities ending in -ese take the and no -s: the Japanese.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'I know lots of ___.' (GERMANY)
exercises.explanation: German ends in -an, so we add -s: Germans.

exercises.statement: I met a lot of Russians on my trip to Moscow.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Russian ends in -an, so the plural is Russians, with no the.
